title: Open-Source MBTI Test (OEJTS 1.2): 32 Questions & Scorer
description: How the Open Extended Jungian Type Scales (OEJTS 1.2) works: all 32 bipolar items, midpoint scoring, tie-breaking rules, and free test.
h1: Open-source MBTI-style test (OEJTS 1.2): 32 items and scorer.
dek: How the 32-item Open Extended Jungian Type Scales work, how axis margins and ties are calculated, and why tie-breaking rules change AI model headlines.
lede: The Open Extended Jungian Type Scales (OEJTS 1.2), developed by Eric Jorgenson for the Open Psychometrics Project, is the standard open-science alternative to proprietary four-letter type questionnaires. On AgentTune, our browser adaptation runs locally at /tests/mbti with zero account sign-up and a transparent, deterministic JavaScript scorer.
answer: The OEJTS 1.2 uses 32 bipolar items rated 1 to 5 between two opposite statements, with 8 items per axis: Extraversion/Introversion (E/I), Sensing/Intuition (S/N), Thinking/Feeling (T/F), and Judging/Perceiving (J/P). Each axis has a constant sum of 48 across its 8 items, so 24 vs 24 (a signed margin of 0) is an exact tie. AgentTune's scorer reports both the signed axis margins and tie-preserving codes (marking tied axes as X) alongside optional tie-broken four-letter types.

sections.html:
Unlike agreement-scale questionnaires where every statement is rated from Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree, each OEJTS item places two contrasting descriptions at opposite ends of a 1-to-5 scale. Eight items measure each of the four Jungian preference axes:

AxisTwo polesItemsAxis sum & tie point
E / IExtraversion vs Introversion8 bipolar items (1–5)Pole sum = 48; exact tie at 24 vs 24 (margin 0)
S / NSensing vs Intuition8 bipolar items (1–5)Pole sum = 48; exact tie at 24 vs 24 (margin 0)
T / FThinking vs Feeling8 bipolar items (1–5)Pole sum = 48; exact tie at 24 vs 24 (margin 0)
J / PJudging vs Perceiving8 bipolar items (1–5)Pole sum = 48; exact tie at 24 vs 24 (margin 0)

In the shared scorer at /resources/scoring/score.js, each item contributes to its two poles so that the two pole totals on any axis always add up to 48, and the signed margin (for example, I - E or N - S) ranges from -16 to +16 in even steps of 2. When a person or an AI model picks the midpoint (3) on all eight items of an axis, or balances left and right responses equally, both poles equal 24 and the signed margin is 0.

sections.h2: Why tie handling changes AI personality results.
sections.html:
Conventional web quizzes never show a five-character or X-masked result: when an axis ties at 24 to 24, a strict > comparison silently awards the letter to whichever pole sits in the else branch (in our earlier study scripts, I, N, T, and J). In our September 2026 reanalysis (How tie-breaking changes AI MBTI results), keeping tied axes open as X revealed substantial boundary clustering:

sections.h2: Sample INTJ / ISTJ analytical communication block.
sections.html:
If you already know your four-letter preference and want to skip straight to tuning your assistant, copy this structured analytical block or pick your exact type in the library:

## Communication preferences - Lead with the conclusion, model, or recommendation in the first sentence. - Organize multi-part answers around clear causal structure and explicit assumptions. - Use plain prose by default; use tables only when comparing three or more alternatives. - Skip small talk, flattery, and closing filler. - Point out logical gaps or unverified premises before executing a plan.

faq.q: What is the OEJTS 1.2 personality test?
faq.a: The Open Extended Jungian Type Scales (OEJTS 1.2) is a 32-item open-science questionnaire developed by the Open Psychometrics Project to measure four Jungian preference axes (E/I, S/N, T/F, and J/P) on a 1-to-5 bipolar scale.

faq.q: How does OEJTS 1.2 handle tied scores?
faq.a: Each of the four axes has 8 items whose two poles sum to 48, making 24 vs 24 an exact tie. AgentTune's scorer reports tied axes explicitly with an X (such as IXTJ) rather than silently forcing a tie-break toward I, N, T, or J.

faq.q: Is the AgentTune OEJTS test free and private?
faq.a: Yes. The test at /tests/mbti runs entirely in your browser tab with no email capture, no account creation, and no server upload of your individual answers.

faq.q: Can I use the OEJTS specification to test an LLM?
faq.a: Yes. You can fetch the Markdown specification at /tests/mbti.md, score responses deterministically with /resources/scoring/score.js, and compare against our frozen 400-session dataset in the research hub.
